Best approximation

Finding the closest feasible point

New operator designs for Halpern iterations with explicit rates under Hölder error bounds

P. Barros, V. Guigues, R. Behling, L.-R. Santos.

Mathematics of Computation

When many constraints must hold at once, how can we find the feasible solution closest to a given reference point?

A feasibility method can find a point satisfying every constraint without selecting the closest one. Halpern iteration adds a vanishing pull toward the original reference point. This anchor turns a broad family of projection operators into methods for best approximation.

Main result

We establish convergence to the metric projection and explicit rates for feasibility and distance to that projection under Hölder error bounds. The geometry of the intersection determines the rates.

Where it matters

Constrained reconstruction

Constrained reconstruction: adjust a noisy estimate as little as possible while enforcing convex consistency constraints. The paper tests best approximation over intersections of ellipsoids and polyhedra.

doi.org/10.1090/mcom/4267
Parallel affine feasibility

Letting geometry combine parallel work

Parallelizing the circumcentered reflection method

P. Barros, R. Behling, V. Guigues, L.-R. Santos.

Preprint · Under review

Can we use several processors to solve affine constraints while preserving the geometry that makes circumcenter methods effective?

Reflect the current point across several affine subspaces independently, then combine those reflected points through their circumcenter: the point in their affine hull equally distant from each. The independent reflection work can run in parallel.

Main result

For affine subspaces with nonempty intersection, P-CRM converges linearly to the projection of the initial point onto the intersection. Its analysis also compares it with simultaneous projections.

Where it matters

Large linear systems

Large systems of linear constraints, including projection onto the solution set of a consistent linear system. Groups of equations can be handled independently before the circumcenter combines their information.

arXiv:2505.17258
Convex feasibility · 3PM / A3PM

Turning curved constraints into useful cuts

Parallel polyhedral projection method for the convex feasibility problem

P. Barros, V. Guigues, R. Behling.

Preprint · Under review

How can we combine information from many convex constraints in a single productive step?

Project onto the individual sets in parallel. Each projection supplies a supporting half-space containing the feasible intersection. Projecting onto their intersection uses all this local geometric information at once. A3PM allows controlled approximations in these operations.

Main result

The methods converge globally without a regularity assumption. Error bounds give linear rates, and additional geometric conditions yield superlinear convergence for 3PM.

Where it matters

Reconstruction with many constraints

Convex constraint satisfaction in reconstruction and estimation. Different measurements or physical restrictions define separate convex sets; supporting half-spaces provide a tractable outer approximation of their common feasible region.

arXiv:2506.15895
Two-set feasibility · ecCRM

Designing a better launch point

Deep centralization for the circumcentered reflection method

P. Barros.

Preprint · Under review

Can a more carefully chosen centralization step make circumcenter updates more effective?

ecCRM replaces a fixed centralization rule with an admissible operator T and a parameter α. A deeper operator composes additional projections before the circumcenter step; a varying α gives another way to control the update.

Main result

The framework preserves global convergence and linear rates under regularity, with superlinearity under additional smooth geometric assumptions. Matrix-completion and ellipsoid experiments demonstrate the practical value of the operator and parameter choices.

Where it matters

Matrix completion

Positive-semidefinite matrix completion: recover a matrix that both matches observed entries and satisfies a structural constraint. These are two different sets, so the method can alternate their projections and exploit circumcenter geometry.

arXiv:2512.05324
Adaptive optimization

Taking advantage of consistent gradients

FlexGrad: A Root-Free Approach to Adaptive Step Sizes

P. Barros, A. Defazio, V. Guigues.

Preprint · Under review

If gradients keep pointing in the same direction, should an adaptive optimizer keep shrinking its steps?

Squared gradients measure magnitude but lose directional information. FlexGrad uses both cumulative gradients and cumulative squared gradients. Persistent directions can support larger steps, while noisy sequences retain AdaGrad-like behavior, without an auxiliary search procedure.

Main result

For convex Lipschitz objectives, the global and coordinate-wise variants attain the optimal asymptotic rate for nonsmooth convex optimization. Experiments examine convex and nonconvex problems.

Where it matters

Adaptive model training

First-order optimization for machine learning. The method adapts to the gradient information available during training, making directional persistence a useful signal for choosing step sizes.

arXiv:2610.09203
Dual dynamic programming · FDDP

Learning the cost of future decisions

Dimension-free complexity guarantees for dual dynamic programming

P. Barros, V. Guigues, J. Liang, R. D. C. Monteiro.

Preprint · Under review

Can we analyze dynamic programming without an iteration bound that grows exponentially with the number of state variables?

Approximate each cost-to-go function from below using affine cuts. The FDDP framework permits flexible model updates, including classical multi-cut models and a memory-efficient variant retaining two cuts per stage. Smoothing and penalization extend the analysis to linearly coupled convex problems.

Main result

We derive dimension-independent iteration-complexity bounds with the other problem constants held fixed. Individual subproblem solves can still become more expensive as the state dimension increases.

Where it matters

Multistage resource planning

Large deterministic planning problems with decisions coupled across stages, such as inventory or resource allocation. A compact model of future cost helps avoid solving the entire horizon as one large problem.

arXiv:2606.10203
Stochastic dynamic programming · BSDDP

Using repeated scenarios to refine decisions

Bidirectional SDDP with dimension-free complexity for solving strongly convex stochastic dynamic programming equations

P. Barros, V. Guigues.

Preprint · Under review

How does strong convexity help us understand the effort needed to make decisions over an uncertain horizon?

BSDDP stores trial points along sampled scenario paths. When a full path is sampled again, the method uses its previous trial points and the current path's realizations to update cost-to-go models before the forward decisions.

Main result

Under the paper's assumptions, the expected iteration bound for an approximately optimal first-stage decision with optimal recourse is independent of state dimension when the other constants are fixed. Path probabilities and the horizon remain part of the bound.

Where it matters

Planning under uncertain demand

Sequential planning under uncertainty, such as reservoir management or inventory control. A decision today changes tomorrow's state, while future inflows or demand remain uncertain.

arXiv:2606.10161
Decision-dependent stochastic models

Following an equilibrium that keeps moving

Tracking Time-Varying Equilibria in Decision-Dependent Stochastic Variational Inequalities

P. Barros, Z. Harchaoui, V. Guigues.

Expected submission · Jan 2027

What happens when our decisions change the data distribution, and the equilibrium itself changes over time?

A variational inequality describes equilibrium through an operator rather than a single minimization objective. In a decision-dependent model, the choice also affects the distribution generating observations. Time variation adds a moving target to this feedback loop.

Research direction

This project studies how extragradient-type methods track evolving equilibria and how tracking error relates to environmental change. The manuscript is in preparation.

Where it matters

Adaptive markets and model deployment

Adaptive pricing or deployment of predictive models: actions can influence demand or the population of future observations. Tracking a changing equilibrium can be more relevant than solving one fixed optimization problem.

Stabilized stochastic programming

Making early planning steps more stable

Regularized SDDP via trust-region stabilization for multistage stochastic programs

V. Guigues, V. Leclère, P. Barros, A. Shapiro.

Expected submission · Mar 2027

How can we keep early decisions useful when our approximation of future cost is still rough?

SDDP learns future costs through cutting-plane models. Early models may be inaccurate far from the states already explored. A trust region restricts a trial decision to a neighborhood of a reference point, controlling how far the method moves while those models improve.

Research direction

This project investigates trust-region regularization for multistage stochastic programs. The manuscript is in preparation.

Where it matters

Stable energy and inventory planning

Energy scheduling, inventory, and other repeated planning problems in which large swings between trial decisions can make early exploration inefficient. Stabilization gives a way to control that movement.

A common thread

Use the structure.
Make the computation count.

Across projection geometry, adaptive optimization, and dynamic programming, my work asks how mathematical structure can lead to algorithms with useful guarantees and scalable computation.
